ghi_chu.mo_ta: A tall, slender, pale rectangular tower with a small dark pointed cap stands alone on the skyline. It looks like a modern obelisk or tower block, and it is not a known London structure of the period.
ghi_chu.ly_do: No such tower stood in London in 1675. It does not match any church spire or the Monument, which was still being built and has a column and urn form. It looks like a later or invented landmark.

ghi_chu.mo_ta: The skyline is a long, uniform row of tall red-brick blocks with regular windows and many chimneys. They look like 18th–19th-century terraces or industrial blocks.
ghi_chu.ly_do: London in 1675 was being rebuilt after the 1666 fire. Its buildings were mostly timber-framed or early brick houses with gables, and they were lower and more varied than this regular row of tall blocks.
